subject: Kestrel: Dedicated capacity next-steps and GPU priorities
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@kestrel.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kestrel kickoff — quick recap and action items

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a few concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Deployment preference: you flagged Dedicated capacity as the likely path due to steady high-volume inference and data isolation needs (no VPC required today).
- Primary workload: multi-turn customer chat + summary generation; average request ~420 tokens in, 200 tokens out; 95th percentile prompt length ~1,200 tokens during peak workflows.
- TPS target: you said 60 steady TPS during peak business hours with short bursts up to ~120 TPS for 5–10 minute windows.
- Concurrency: expected ~12 concurrent long-lived sessions (chat with KV caching) plus ~120 short inference calls per second for async batch-style features.
- Quality constraint: model must preserve context windows for 4–6 turns; quantization OK if no >8% quality regression on our eval set.

Next steps (owners):
1) Jasmine: send token mix CSV and an initial dedicated-capacity estimate (GPU flavors & baseline throughput) — attached.
2) Kestrel: confirm burst pattern cadence (how often/day) and expected retention of conversation state (seconds/minutes) by EOD Wed.
3) Redwood: propose a two-sku plan (high-throughput GPU + fallback lower-cost GPU) and optional routing rule for bursts.

Attachments: kestrel_token_profile.csv (token mix sample), dedicated_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx (initial roughs)

If any of the bullets above are off, flag and I'll correct. Assuming Dedicated is right, I'll loop in Karthik for the GPU+concurrency proposal tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | rediscover inference economics

From: Samir Patel <samir@kestrel.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@kestrel.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel kickoff — quick recap and action items

Thanks Jasmine — that matches my notes. Two clarifications before you size: 

1) Bursts: the 120 TPS bursts are triggered by promotional emails roughly 4x/day, each burst ~7 minutes on avg. Outside those bursts traffic is steady around 40–60 TPS.
2) Stateful retention: we need session-level KV cached context for up to 20 minutes for premium users; non-premium can be stateless. Premium users make up ~18% of traffic but are 60% of token consumption.

Also cc'd contracts to start a high level T&Cs review; we'll likely request a 90-day pilot with a minimum committed throughput.

Appreciate the estimate — ping me when you have the GPU options.

—Samir
Head of Platform, Kestrel Analytics

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Kestrel kickoff — sizing inputs (for GPU recommendation)

Karthik/Ben — forwarding Samir's clarifications. Key new items: 4 bursts/day ~7min @120 TPS; premium users require 20m KV retention (18% traffic, 60% tokens). I've attached their token profile and a quick estimate file. Please see questions below and draft a two-sku recommendation we can present to the customer (include expected latency at P50/P95 and per-token cost delta).

Questions for sizing:
- GPU flavors to propose: prefer mix of A100-40GB (cost-effective) + H100 (for headroom) or recommend L40s for better price/throughput? Include notes on KV cache memory impact per session.
- Batching strategy: suggest steady-state batching target for 60 TPS and separate fast-path for burst handling — what concurrency settings should we expose as customer-configurable?
- Fallback routing: propose automatic fallback to lower-cost model when queue depth > X or latency > Y ms. What thresholds are safe without severe quality regression?

Attachments: kestrel_token_profile.csv, dedicated_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx

Thanks — can you do a short write-up by 11:30 so I can send to Samir before EOD?

Jasmine
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Kestrel kickoff — sizing inputs (for GPU recommendation)

Quick proposal notes (will expand into slide + calc):

- Sku A (baseline): 4x A100-40GB nodes, continuous throughput target 65 TPS, estimated P95 latency ~220ms for 620-token outputs with batching 1–4; handles premium KV retention by reserving 8–10GB KV memory per GPU (eviction policy recommended).
- Sku B (performance): 2x H100 nodes fronted via smart-router for burst capacity; can absorb short 120 TPS bursts using autoscale/burst pool with max queue depth tuned to 30; P95 latency ~140ms under burst when scaled.
- Fallback: route to quantized Llama-variant on L40 if queue depth >40 or per-request latency >1200ms for >5s. Expect ~6–8% quality delta — flag this clearly to Samir.
- Concurrency config to expose: max_concurrency_per_gpu (start 48), batch_interval_ms (10–20), kv_retention_seconds (1200 for premium).

I'll run cost proforma and token-cost deltas for both skus and upload to the Drive link. Recommend we present the two-sku option plus an ops playbook: burst routing, cache sizing, and an ALLOWED fallback policy for <=90-day pilot.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@kestrel.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@kestrel.ai
Date: 2027-05-04T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel kickoff — quick recap and action items

This looks good — appreciate the fast turnaround. We approve the two-sku approach in principle. Two asks before we proceed to pilot paperwork: 
1) Can you include a short note on expected cost per 1M tokens for each SKU (with and without L40 fallback)?
2) Provide a recommended SLA/uptime target for Dedicated pilot (we prefer 99.5% but open to options tied to burst windows).

If you can get those by EOD Friday, contracting will schedule a pilot review next week.

Thanks,
Samir
